beats.title: Different views
beats.narration_text: When two people face each other, they see different views. One may follow the other's gaze and look for the same object. Could a robot do something similar?

beats.title: What is EyeSpan?
beats.narration_text: EyeSpan is my proposed gaze-guided assistive robot system for tabletop object selection. It is intended for people with limited arm movement. The system will map their gaze target into the robot's view, request confirmation, then guide grasping.

beats.title: Why go further?
beats.narration_text: RaycastGrasp matched objects across views by category, with screenshots and manual cross-checking in my earlier workflow. But two cups share one category. EyeSpan will focus on the particular object and update its estimate continuously, aiming to reduce repeated manual submissions.

beats.title: Intent over time
beats.narration_text: EyeSpan will distinguish stable looking, switching targets, and alternating looks. Stable gaze will accumulate dwell time; a target switch will reset it. Alternating looks below the threshold will keep the system waiting. Reaching the threshold will request confirmation; grasping will require user approval.

beats.title: Evidence and scope
beats.narration_text: I will start with a controlled tabletop and a few stationary objects. Moving-object grasping is outside this stage. Offline mapping checks will not establish successful robot grasping. Evaluation with people with motor impairments remains future work.

beats.title: Concrete failure
beats.narration_text: Look-alike objects may cause wrong-target selection. Smoothing may preserve an error or delay a switch. I will examine both failures and compare stability with switching response. The design will retain explicit confirmation and cancellation before execution.

beats.title: Skills and checks
beats.narration_text: During AI-assisted coding, my prompt contract will define the inputs, target estimate, and selection state. Tests will check missing inputs, invalid coordinates, and unconfirmed execution requests. I will keep the prompts, revisions, and actual results so another person can inspect the checks.

beats.title: Why this project?
beats.narration_text: RaycastGrasp gave me the foundation. EyeSpan asks how a robot can follow a specific target across different views and changing attention. My new course learning will focus on explicit contracts, independent verification, and making a robotics project reproducible for another person.
